stem.en: A hot cup of tea on the table cools to room temperature. It never warms back up on its own. Kabir says "because heat goes from hot to cold, that is a law". What is the reason under the law?

text.en: Heat spread through the room has vastly more ways than heat gathered in the cup. The spread-out arrangement is overwhelmingly more likely, so heat always ends up spread.

feedback.en: Nothing pulls. The molecules bump randomly, and random bumping ends up in the arrangement with the most ways, which is spread out.

text.en: Because the tea is trying to match the room.

feedback.en: Tea does not try. The count of ways does it, one collision at a time.
A sealed steel flask cools too, just slower. The question is why never the other way, and the answer is counting.

explanation.en: "Heat goes from hot to cold" is the rule you observe. Entropy is the reason: the spread-out arrangement has more ways, and more ways means more likely, by a margin with more digits than you could ever write.
